35 Two cells are connected to a load resistor of resistance 3.0 Ω. The electromotive force (e.m.f).
and the internal resistance of each of the cells is shown.
0.8 Ω
1.2 Ω
6.0 V
3.0 V
3.0 Ω
What is the current in the load resistor?
A
0.60 A
B
1.2 A
C
1.8 A
D
3.0 A

hints: Notice how the $6.0 \text{ V}$ cell with $0.8 \text{ } \Omega$, the $3.0 \text{ V}$ cell with $1.2 \text{ } \Omega$, and the $3.0 \text{ } \Omega$ load form one single series loop.
Check whether the two cells aid or oppose by tracing round the loop: the positive of one connects to the negative of the other, so their e.m.f.s add as $6.0+3.0$.
Add all three resistances for the total resistance, then use $I = E_{total}/R_{total}$ with $E$ in $\text{V}$ and $R$ in $\Omega$.
walkthrough: Identify the loop: current must pass in turn through the $0.8 \text{ } \Omega$ internal resistance, the $1.2 \text{ } \Omega$ internal resistance and the $3.0 \text{ } \Omega$ load, so all three are in series.
Decide on total e.m.f.: the cells are connected positive-to-negative in the same rotational sense, so they aid. Hence $E_{total} = 6.0 + 3.0 = 9.0 \text{ V}$.
Apply $I = E_{total}/R_{total}$ for a series circuit with internal resistance: $I = 9.0/5.0 = 1.8 \text{ A}$.
This current is the same everywhere in series, so it is the current in the $3.0 \text{ } \Omega$ load. This is option C.

A.explanation: Gives $0.60 \text{ A}$ from $(6.0-3.0)/5.0$, which treats the $6.0 \text{ V}$ and $3.0 \text{ V}$ cells as opposing rather than aiding in series.

B.explanation: Gives $1.2 \text{ A}$ from $6.0/5.0$, which uses only the $6.0 \text{ V}$ cell and omits the $3.0 \text{ V}$ contribution.

C.explanation: Gives $9.0/5.0 = 1.8 \text{ A}$ from total e.m.f. $6.0+3.0$ and total resistance $0.8+1.2+3.0$ in series.

D.explanation: Gives $3.0 \text{ A}$ from $9.0/3.0$, which omits the $0.8 \text{ } \Omega$ and $1.2 \text{ } \Omega$ internal resistances.
